object_description: compact low-rise volume articulated by shifts and four patios
design_condition: The compact volume is placed at the edge of the urban composition, with cut-out faces reacting to the context; its low height preserves neighboring views, while the design fails to engage sufficiently with the existing slope.

positive.statement: The finely articulated building asserts itself vigorously while fitting accurately into the urban composition.
Shifts in the compact volume subtly organize the ground floor and link it to the exterior spaces.
The resulting spaces offer diversity and can be appropriated by students and the population.
The organization of access and public activities allows events outside school hours to function smoothly.
The circulation spaces are subtly hierarchical, generous, and varied in atmosphere.
Views and natural light are provided at corridor ends and around the interior courtyards.
The distribution of the program across the floors is consistent.
The interior circulation resembles a small school medina and counteracts the mass effect of the large school.
The organization supports the educational and socialization mission of the establishment.
The construction system is simple and efficient, combining a main structure with localized rigid cores.
The proposal is the most efficient among the presented projects from an energy and sustainability perspective.
Eaves, passageways, and patios provide protection from noise and summer sun.
The proposal has strong potential for optimization without distorting its architectural qualities.

negative.statement: The landscape concept lacks character and definition compared with the architectural and urban design.
The open-ground surfaces should offer more freshness, biodiversity, and varied appropriation.
The basement organization needs adaptations to address dysfunctions and allow vegetation in at least one patio.
The multimedia room must be treated as a classroom and receive daylight.
The vertical distribution and number of sanitary blocks appear insufficient for the number of students per floor.
The documentation center premises must be directly accessible from the media library.
The arrangement of classrooms opposite each other across patios raises concerns.
Access for the spectators to the stands is unsatisfactory and must allow exchanges between sides without passing through the sports hall or outside.
Publicly accessible areas must be partitionable from the strictly school spaces.
The basement plan is ineffective and problematic, particularly because of vertical distributions and mixed uses.
The location of the equipment-room access through the stands cannot work, and the refreshment bar and toilets must connect to the public stands.
The outdoor sports fields and running track should be located away from classroom facades.
The parking layout takes priority over the relationship between the street and the school complex.
The envelope and entrances should offer more varied intermediate spaces between enclosed areas and natural elements.
Two patios are limited to providing natural lighting and should acquire a stronger quality of use.
The project ignores the existing topography.
The exterior arrangements require more sustained and sensitive attention.
The parking and municipal-program layouts should be reviewed, and more space should be provided along the quieter frontage.
Ventilation and heat production remain insufficiently developed.
Exterior solar protection is needed to avoid summer overheating.
The teaching rooms on one frontage are highly exposed to road noise.
The proportion of glazing should be reduced to improve environmental performance and comfort.
